title: Set the tax

predict.q: MPB = MSB = 100 − Q; MPC = 20 + Q; MEC = 20, so MSC = 40 + Q. The government sets the tax at **30**, above the MEC. What happens to the welfare loss?

options.s: It falls to zero: a higher tax is always better
options.fb: Above the MEC, the tax pushes output below Q*. Units worth more than their full social cost are no longer made: a new welfare loss.

options.s: A new welfare loss appears: output falls below Q*
options.fb: Output falls to 25, below Q* = 30: a new (underproduction) welfare loss of 25.
The tax raises firms' costs by more, so supply shifts further and output falls below Q*.

task: Move the **tax** slider from 0 to 40 and watch output and the welfare loss.

target.do: Set the tax to 30, then press Check.

takeaway: The tax must **match** the MEC. Too low leaves overproduction; too high causes **underproduction**.
